hints: Replace N with the supplied base-unit form before multiplying by m.
Collect the two metre factors.

walkthrough.text: Energy transferred has unit J = N m.
Substitute N = kg m s^-2 to obtain J = (kg m s^-2)m.
Collect the metre factors: J = kg m^2 s^-2.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses J = N m and substitutes kg m s^-2 for N
Simplifies the joule to kg m^2 s^-2

evidence.role: The mapped leaf grounds comparing complete SI base-unit forms across an equation; the sum, symbols and options are original

hints: Simplify every term separately.
A sum is valid only when both terms and the left side have the same unit.

walkthrough.text: The left side x has unit m.
For option C, vt has unit (m s^-1)(s) = m.
The second term at^2 has unit (m s^-2)(s^2) = m.
Both right-hand terms match x, so option C is homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects x = vt + at^2 as the homogeneous equation

evidence.role: The mapped leaves ground using a supplied force model to identify whether a coefficient needs units; the model notation and options are original

hints: Combine density, area and squared speed first.
Compare the result with the force unit before assigning a unit to C.

walkthrough.text: Substitute the units without C: (kg m^-3)(m^2)(m s^-1)^2.
This becomes (kg m^-3)(m^2)(m^2 s^-2) = kg m s^-2.
The result already matches the force unit, so C needs no unit and option A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects no unit because rho A u^2 already reduces to kg m s^-2

evidence.role: The mapped leaf directly grounds equating length exponents in a supplied geometric relationship; the quantity names and prompt are original

hints: Write the right-hand unit as kg m^n divided by m.
Match the final metre exponent to -3.

walkthrough.text: The right side has unit (kg)(m^n)/m = kg m^(n-1).
For homogeneity, kg m^-3 = kg m^(n-1).
Equate metre powers: -3 = n - 1, so n = -2 and option B is correct.
Check: n = -2 makes the right side kg m^(-2-1) = kg m^-3.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects n = -2 by matching kg m^-3 to kg m^(n-1)

hints: Keep the cube attached to the whole speed unit.

Compare that product with the stated unit of S in part (b).
Repeat the simplification with only two speed factors for part (c), then identify the exact mismatch.

evidence.role: Grounds full base-unit simplification of a multi-factor product

hints: Cube both the metre and inverse-second factors in u.
Cancel the m^-3 from density against the m^3 from speed cubed.

walkthrough.text: Write [rho u^3] = (kg m^-3)(m s^-1)^3.
Cube the speed unit: (m s^-1)^3 = m^3 s^-3.
Multiply to obtain (kg m^-3)(m^3 s^-3) = kg s^-3.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes (kg m^-3)(m s^-1)^3 for rho u^3
Simplifies rho u^3 to kg s^-3

evidence.role: Grounds the final comparison of independently simplified sides

hints: Carry the part (a) unit into the right side.
A unitless C does not change the base-unit form.

walkthrough.text: The left side has the stated unit [S] = kg s^-3.
From part (a), [rho u^3] = kg s^-3, and C contributes no unit.
The two sides match, so the proposed model is homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Compares kg s^-3 on the left with kg s^-3 on the right
Concludes that S = C rho u^3 is homogeneous

evidence.role: Extends the grounded factor comparison to diagnose an original altered exponent

hints: Square the entire speed unit.
Compare both the metre and second powers with S.

walkthrough.text: The altered product is [rho u^2] = (kg m^-3)(m s^-1)^2.
This simplifies to (kg m^-3)(m^2 s^-2) = kg m^-1 s^-2.
The result differs from kg s^-3 in both metre and time powers, so the second equation is not homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Simplifies rho u^2 to kg m^-1 s^-2
Concludes that the u^2 proposal is not homogeneous because kg m^-1 s^-2 does not match kg s^-3

hints: Keep K and K^-1 visible until they cancel.

Cancel the temperature units and simplify the length quotient before comparing with E.
For the altered model, divide the already simplified right side by s and compare again.

evidence.role: Grounds complete simplification involving a supplied constant, area or volume factors, temperature and length

hints: Substitute the five supplied unit factors in the same order as the equation.
Cancel K first, then divide the metre powers.

walkthrough.text: Write the right-hand unit as [(kg s^-2 K^-1)(m^3)(K)]/m.
The temperature powers cancel because K^-1 x K = 1.
The length quotient is m^3/m = m^2.
The full result is kg m^2 s^-2.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes (kg s^-2 K^-1)(m^3)(K)/m into the right-hand side
Cancels K^-1 with K and divides m^3 by m
Simplifies the right-hand side to kg m^2 s^-2

evidence.role: Grounds comparing the completed base-unit result with the left-hand quantity

hints: Carry the simplified unit from part (a).
Compare it with the stated unit of E.

The left side E also has unit kg m^2 s^-2.
Therefore the supplied model is homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that the model is homogeneous because both sides reduce to kg m^2 s^-2

evidence.role: Extends the grounded thermal unit comparison to diagnose an original extra time factor

hints: Start from the right-hand result in part (a).
Dividing by time is multiplying by s^-1.

walkthrough.text: The original right side has unit kg m^2 s^-2.
Dividing by an additional t contributes s^-1, giving kg m^2 s^-3.
This differs from [E] = kg m^2 s^-2, so the altered equation is not homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Determines the altered right-hand unit as kg m^2 s^-3
Concludes that the altered equation is not homogeneous because kg m^2 s^-3 does not match kg m^2 s^-2

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground energy and power base-unit derivation, output per area and complete side comparison; the meter and second proposal are original

hints: Build the power unit before testing either model.
Divide by area and length separately rather than comparing them by appearance.

walkthrough.text: Use the previous lesson's force-energy-power route in part (a).
Carry kg m^2 s^-3 into part (b), divide by m^2 and compare with S.
For part (c), divide the same power unit by only m and state exactly what the mismatch proves.

evidence.role: Directly grounds deriving energy and power in SI base-unit form

hints: Begin with the base-unit form of force.
After finding the energy unit, divide by one second.

walkthrough.text: Force has base-unit form kg m s^-2.
Energy = force x distance, so [energy] = (kg m s^-2)(m) = kg m^2 s^-2.
Power = energy/time, so [P] = (kg m^2 s^-2)/s = kg m^2 s^-3.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses kg m s^-2 for force in the supplied force-times-distance route
Derives the energy unit as kg m^2 s^-2
Divides by s to derive the power unit kg m^2 s^-3

evidence.role: Grounds converting power per area to a complete output unit and comparing the two sides

hints: Use the part (a) power unit.
A has unit m^2 and C contributes no unit.

walkthrough.text: Carry [P] = kg m^2 s^-3 from part (a).
Then [CP/A] = (1)(kg m^2 s^-3)/m^2 = kg s^-3.
This matches [S], so S = CP/A is homogeneous.

ai_rubric.observable: Simplifies CP/A to kg s^-3 using C dimensionless and A in m^2
Concludes that S = CP/A is homogeneous because both sides have unit kg s^-3

evidence.role: Grounds a complete quotient simplification while the original length denominator and conclusion are newly authored

hints: Divide the part (a) power unit by one metre.
A mismatch lets you reject the equation as written, but no stronger conclusion is needed.

walkthrough.text: Use [P] = kg m^2 s^-3 and [L] = m.
Then [CP/L] = (1)(kg m^2 s^-3)/m = kg m s^-3.
The left side has unit kg s^-3, so the metre powers do not match.
Therefore S = CP/L cannot be correct as written.

ai_rubric.observable: Simplifies CP/L to kg m s^-3
Concludes that S = CP/L cannot be correct as written because kg m s^-3 does not match kg s^-3

quality_audit.originality: All learner contexts, wording, symbols, altered equations and planned diagrams are original. No official numerical data, wording or figure layout is reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The lesson teaches only how to use SI base units to check equation homogeneity, determine a required power or constant unit, and state the limited meaning of a unit match.
quality_audit.evidence: All seven mapped P2 leaves and all six complete source-question contexts were reviewed. They ground multi-factor checks, dimensionless coefficients, unknown exponents, charge or temperature base-unit factors, and linked energy-power routes. P1 evidence is deferred and was not inferred.
later_knowledge_excluded: later-topic physical principles beyond the supplied unit-analysis context
